Messages.Author: kschaefer
Messages.Body:
I've been toying with Black Hand/Under Siege, too. I think the permanents or semi-permanents allow for very toolbox designs. Not sure what your metagame is like, but here are a few thoughts:

You only have two vampires that can play Under Seige. Consider Jefferson Foster or Polly Kay Fisher to up the titles to make US a more reliable play. Aaron Bathhurst is supposed to be someone else or simply removed.

Hungry Coyote with all that Theft of Vitae? Seems like two pool you'd rather put elsewhere like a Guardian Angel for some permanent prevent. No Remover? No Pentex Subversion?

Do you expect to be in torpor and if so, do you not expect Recure to be blocked? That card is cool in theory, but never seems to make the cut. Not sure about the rest of the actions, but I'm trying not to turn this into the deck I've built.

You only have two post-declaration pieces of bleed boost and what you do have is Bonding. This package needs more punch. If you can get one bleed through in a turn, you want it to be for more than two. Seduction to help these hit more frequently? Is Mirror Walks stealth enough for your meta? With the combat, you have I'm not sure I'd expect you to use the cancel combat effect, making Seduction even more useful in case of bounced bleeds.

What's combat like in you area? This package seems too large for a deck without rushes and Fames. I'd cut the TT and Walk of Flame. Your focus on BH vampires makes Psychic Assault (unpreventable when played by BH), a nice punch on top of the Thefts. I'd expect to want fewer "good" combats than you. This deck needs to survive and occasionally punish, but this package is just too large.

For the equipment consider Codex of Edenic Groundskeepers. You're not really doing stealth anyway.

This reaction package needs bleed bounce. You have access to both disciplines for it. I'd prefer a mix of Murmur (depending on the average cap in your meta), Deflection, MEE, and TM.

Messages.Author: Kraus
Messages.Body:
I'm playing 70-80 card decks, or aim for those numbers. The fun part is that it doesn't matter if you draw it late or early, it gives roughly the equal amount of value and uses anyways.

So, I'd say realistically (depending on your cycle) you get 6-7 tutors per game? With the maximum of 10-11 of course, but at that time you're depleted of your deck anyways and the tutor effect isn't useful anymore.

For JUST the right combat card, the ousting Conditioning or saving bounce, it's totally worth it. Just a better Barrens, in a sense. Combos nicely with Barrens as well though.
